checked.title: Two-stage approval: Expert Mode deterministic rules first, local-model classifier second ("auto mode" without the cloud tax)
checked.evidence: libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/auto_mode.py:32-46 (AutoDecision/RuleVerdict, rule_source incl. "haiku"), :208-228 HaikuEvalConfig (enabled=True, model claude-haiku-4-5), :230-241 AutoModeSettings.enabled defaults False, :455-489 haiku_risk_eval hard-imports `anthropic` and fails closed ("anthropic package unavailable — treating as risky"), returns bool not a risk grade; libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/textual_adapter.py:757-800 _evaluate_auto_mode_batch runs rule engine then Haiku only on rule_source=="default"; app.py:5712-5760 `/auto` is on|off|status only; app.py:16010-16030 default permission mode is "default" (prompt-all), auto = "accept-edits"; app.py:12157-12165 `/why` routes only to expert_controller (tool_call facts, expert_rules.py:333); libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/middleware/smart_approvals.py:32-40,148-283 SDK RiskLevel policies are regex/heuristic, no model call; tests: libs/cli/tests/unit_tests/test_auto_mode_rules.py (56 tests; only :375 covers haiku config — no test found driving haiku_risk_eval or _evaluate_auto_mode_batch). No hits for circuit.?breaker|recently denied|critique|containment.
checked.delta: (1) Make accept-edits/auto the default permission mode (today `default` prompts for everything and AutoModeSettings.enabled=False). (2) Replace the hard-wired `import anthropic` in haiku_risk_eval with an injected `invoke` (model_config factory) so the reviewer can be Ollama/Bedrock/any provider — today non-Anthropic installs fail closed straight to HITL. (3) Return structured {risk: low|medium|high|critical, rationale} and map critical→deny, high→HITL, low→approve (today boolean risky). (4) Prose policy file (.bog-agents/auto-mode.md) with allow/soft_deny/hard_deny/environment sections + `$defaults` splice replacing the regex lists in settings.json. (5) `bog-agents auto-mode defaults|config|critique|reset` headless twins (headless_commands.py). (6) 'Recently denied' tab with retry in the TUI. (7) Per-turn denial circuit breaker (N denials → escalate to human). (8) Containment-Escape default rule (cloud metadata endpoints, proxy/egress evasion) in _DEFAULT_SHELL_ASK_PATTERNS. (9) Feed RuleVerdict + reviewer rationale into the expert engine as a fact so `/why` explains auto-mode denials with the proof trace. Add tests for haiku_risk_eval and the batch evaluator.
checked.competitor: Claude Code (auto mode default Aug 14; prose rules + `claude auto-mode critique`; Containment Escape Sep 1) and Codex (Guardian auto-review with policy.md, circuit breaker, `/approve`)
checked.why_killer: Users stop rubber-stamping 97% of prompts (Anthropic's own number) yet keep a deterministic, auditable floor the competitors lack: an enterprise can prove which rule fired, a solo user on a laptop runs the reviewer on a local 8B model for free and offline, and both get the classifier's long-tail coverage. ROADMAP #23 proposed risk-graded reviewer approvals; the bar moved because both leaders now ship it as the DEFAULT with a prose-rule DSL, a critique/lint CLI and a denial-retry UI — bog must match that surface, not just the concept.

checked.title: Native Windows sandbox via restricted tokens + WFP firewall (Codex's design), wired into LocalShellBackend
checked.evidence: libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/sandbox/local_sandbox.py:57-100 SandboxSupport.detect probes only `bwrap` (linux) and `sandbox-exec` (darwin); :94-97 docstring: "Windows has no launcher yet (AppContainer wiring is tracked as ROADMAP #22)"; libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/backends/local_shell.py:10-11,195,320,583 `require_sandbox=True` fails closed "where no native launcher is available (e.g. Windows today)"; libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/sandbox/egress_proxy.py:138 AllowlistEgressProxy exists (usable as the 'online' user's egress); libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/exec_risk.py: 0 matches for powershell|pwsh|EncodedCommand; tests exist only for bwrap/seatbelt paths (libs/bog-agents/tests/unit_tests/test_local_sandbox_*.py).
checked.delta: Implement a Windows launcher in local_sandbox.py: unelevated mode = CreateRestrictedToken (WRITE_RESTRICTED + synthetic SID) from the current user with explicit ACL grants on working_dir/temp/caches/`writable_roots` from sandbox.toml (document the Everyone-SID gap); elevated mode = provision two low-privilege local users (offline: WFP block-all rule; online: egress forced through the existing AllowlistEgressProxy) and CreateProcessAsUser; wire `SandboxSupport.detect` windows branch + `SandboxConfig.build_local_sandbox`; add a PowerShell AST inspection pass to exec_risk.py (`-EncodedCommand`, `Invoke-Expression`, dynamic script blocks → veto auto-approval); reparse-point (junction/symlink) hardening on writable roots; docs on what is kernel-enforced vs proxy-cooperative; Windows CI job running the sandbox conformance tests.
checked.competitor: OpenAI Codex (native Windows sandbox May 14; reparse-point hardening v0.149.0 Aug 20); Claude Code still 'Native Windows is not supported' (issue #46740 closed not-planned); Antigravity claims AppContainer
checked.why_killer: Windows-first users get real OS isolation today (Claude Code tells them to use WSL2; bog's own sandbox fails closed on Windows), and regulated shops get an auditable boundary for auto-approved shell. ROADMAP #22 already flagged Windows as the open flank; the bar moved because Codex proved a working restricted-token + firewall design and rejected AppContainer — bog can copy a validated architecture instead of inventing one, and it remains the only LangGraph-based framework with it.

checked.title: Credential masking at the egress proxy (sentinel secrets substituted only toward allow-listed hosts)
checked.evidence: libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/sandbox/egress_proxy.py:47-330 is a CONNECT-only tunnel (parse_connect_target, _tunnel, _relay/_pump) — no TLS termination, 0 matches for mask|sentinel|credential|inject beyond the `egress_env_for` docstring at :15; libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/sandbox_config.py: 0 matches for credential|mask|inject|envVars; libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/sandbox/local_sandbox.py:126-128,175 `strip_secret_env` only *removes* *SECRET*/*CREDENTIAL* env vars from the child (strip, not substitute); none found after grepping sentinel|inject_hosts|credential_mask|sigv4 outside .venv.
checked.delta: Add `[credentials]` env_vars/files entries with mode=mask to sandbox.toml (SandboxConfig) honored only from user/managed config, never repo-level; generate per-session sentinels and inject them into the sandboxed child's env/files; upgrade the proxy from CONNECT tunnel to a TLS-terminating MITM for `inject_hosts` (per-session CA installed only inside the sandbox env via SSL_CERT_FILE/NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS) that swaps sentinel→real value in headers/bodies, with `extract` substring, JWT-aware `decode`, and AWS SigV4 re-signing; startup check that every masked var has a reachable inject host; surface in `/sandbox` and `/vars`; compose with the DLP middleware so the real value never appears in transcripts/audit trail.
checked.competitor: Claude Code (mask mode for env vars v2.1.199; files + extract/decode/SigV4 v2.1.224, Aug 3-7)
checked.why_killer: Tools like `gh`, `npm`, `aws` keep working inside the sandbox while the agent, its logs, and any exfiltration attempt never hold a real token — the one thing a plain deny list cannot give. Bog already has the proxy and the sandbox.toml; this turns them from a network fence into a secrets boundary that air-gapped/regulated teams can sign off on, and it composes with the DLP middleware.

checked.title: `bog queue` + machine-level session registry + `@session` mentions (cross-session messaging primitive)
checked.evidence: libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/teams.py:162-201 Mailbox is in-process only (threading.Lock over an in-memory list; no persistence); libs/bog-agents/bog_agents/middleware/collaborative_sessions.py:78 sessions held in an in-memory dict; libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/main.py:344-520 subparsers have no `queue`/`agents` subcommand; libs/cli/bog_agents_cli/widgets/autocomplete.py:797-807 _MENTION_TYPES = @file/@folder/@repo/@search/@symbol/@url/@memory/@skill (no @session); none found after grepping session_registry|SessionRegistry|~/.bog-agents/sessions/|notify_when_idle|cross-session; only cross-process entry points are daemon `POST /jobs/{id}/run` (libs/daemon/bog_agents_daemon/api.py:681) and mcp_server.py `run_task`.
checked.delta: Per-machine registry `~/.bog-agents/sessions/<id>.json` (name, cwd, model, state, pid, heartbeat) written by the TUI, daemon runs and serve sessions with auto-unique names; a persistent inbox backend for Mailbox (SQLite or JSONL under the registry) so any process can enqueue; `bog-agents queue --session <name|id> [--file] [--wait]` where --wait streams the next assistant reply; TUI worker checks the inbox at turn boundaries (queue during a turn, wake when idle) and injects the message as a provenance-tagged untrusted HumanMessage that can never satisfy a HITL interrupt; SDK `list_agents`/`send_message` tools with `notify_when_idle`; `@session:` mention type in autocomplete; daemon dispatch target `session:<name>` so cron/CI results land in the session holding the branch.
checked.competitor: Codex `codex queue` + `codex agents` (v0.149.0 Aug 20); Claude Code cross-session messaging (v2.1.224 Aug 3-7, Windows Aug 17-21, `@` mentions v2.1.232)
checked.why_killer: A CI failure, a daemon cron tick, or a teammate's session can drip context into the exact session that already has the branch checked out and the debugging context loaded, instead of a human re-explaining it; teams get loose coupling between sessions with different models/trust profiles, which `/team run` (tight coupling) does not cover. ROADMAP #21/#11 assumed in-process teams and a watch-only dashboard; the bar moved to first-class peer messaging with a CLI entry point, and bog's daemon makes it strictly more useful than either competitor's.

Bog's hook bus is already decision-capable on PreToolUse/Stop; matching the now-standard event set closes the gap users compare against on day one.

checked.title: Security-scan recipe with sandbox-validated findings, FP ledger, `--max-cost`, SARIF and CI gating
